I'm making a new thread to discuss the set-theoretic model of LeanTT, continuing the discussion currently in #lean4lean > State of the Proof. It seems the main points are:

  • If one uses a simpler version of LeanTT (without inductives or something like that), then one can right now formalize the set-theoretic model in Mario's thesis (https://github.com/digama0/lean-type-theory/releases) and the Lean4 update to that model in Sebastian's doctoral dissertation (https://publikationen.bibliothek.kit.edu/1000161074/151088087).
  • The new repo should be separate from Lean4Lean since it needs to depend on Mathlib (to get, say, ZFSet).
  • There was some discussion about putting it in CSLib, but Mario thought that wouldn't be a good idea.

I know I'm a very AI-positive person (annoyingly so), so others may disagree, but seeing the progress on Lean autoformalization, including the Jacobian challenge, it seems that one could very quickly accomplish this with AI help (like in just a few weeks). It seems to me that once the correct theorem statement is constructed, then one has an explicit goal to prove and clear references to consult. In this AI-forward scenario, one can proceed as follows:

  • Make a new repo.
  • Turn the repo into a Comparator project with the main consistency theorem as the target.
  • Use various mechanisms (like a lean blueprint or the markdown files used in the Jacobian challenge solution) to keep track of progress, keep track of to-dos, and farm intermediate goals to agents.
  • Have people who want to help use AI models to fill in missing pieces, and PR filled-in parts back to the repo.

My hope is that once the base consistency proof is accomplished, then it opens doors for other things:

  • Most importantly, one can add in more realistic modifications to LeanTT (including inductives) and adjust the consistency proof accordingly. Or if they are not consistent changes, hopefully this would make it easier to show (with AI help?) that the new resulting model is no longer sound.
  • One can work on more explicit set theory translations. On the set theory side, one could create a direct translation between LeanTT and ZFC+PFIRS (cc @Elliot Glazer) showing that LeanTT |- phi <-> ZFC + PFIRS |- f(phi) where f is a natural translation between propositions of LeanTT and sentences in ZFC. (And one can also show LeanTT |- phi <-> ZFC_omega |- phi for sentences of arithmetic.) This way it is clear that Lean's types-as-sets interpretation is the intended one.
  • One could also consider category theoretic models of LeanTT.
  • More explicit type-theoretic questions can be answered about definitional equality and other things not covered in the set theoretic model. Also, one can work on more proof/type-theoretic proofs of consistency of LeanTT. [Edit: Although I imagine the people interested in this would want their own repo.]

Logistically, how would the maintaince of this simplified fragment work in relation to existing lean4lean? Part of the reason I mentioned CSLib is I mistakenly though it'd be a representation fairly abstracted from the C++ implementation, but this seems not to be the case based on Mario's comments. So when changes do happen to the kernel, this will later get reflected in lean4lean, and then this simplified version?

Yeah, I'm surprised too. Maybe @Mario Carneiro can say more. If one starts with just the type theory in his (and Sebastian's) thesis, then this is certainly abstracted away from the C++, right? The rules are explicitly written in the thesis, if I recall correctly. Is Mario thinking about the future when we add in the actual rules of RealLeanTT, but why can't those also be written down just in type theory notation? It might be good even to have different fragments of LeanTT living in the same place, including toy versions, theoretically ideal versions, and more actual versions. (But maybe I'm totally not understanding.)
How about I make a repo for this and you fill it out? Or maybe I will if I have spare cycles. I basically agree that this will be a relatively quick job for AI
My estimate is more like a day actually, for the main stuff and discounting inductives

one note, the implication is only one way AFAIK, LeanTT |- phi -> ZFC + omega inacc |- f(phi). I have no idea if the reverse holds, and I expect it doesn't without a much more careful model construction
there is another map ZFC + omega inacc |- phi -> LeanTT |- g(phi), and probably the best you can hope for is LeanTT |- phi <-> g(f(phi))

As for the equivalence between LeanTT and ZFC + omega inacc, I would defer mostly to @Elliot Glazer and @James E Hanson (since I haven't yet totally digested it all), but it should go something like this:

  • For arithmetic statements theta: LeanTT |- theta <-> ZFC + omega inacc |- theta.
  • For local statements, there is also a direct conversion. I think one version of this is as follows: for statements phi in the language of the category of sets: LeanTT |- (phi holds in Type n) <-> ZFC + omega inacc |- any inacc kappa with at least n-1 inacc below and l above, (Set_kappa |= phi) where l is sufficiently large. And I think another version is for statements psi in the language of ZFC, LeanTT |- (ZFSet.{n} |= psi) <-> ZFC + omega inacc |- any inacc kappa with at least n-1 inacc below and l above, (V_kappa |= psi) where l is sufficiently large. But to be clear, I might still be getting it wrong. See this stackexchange answer for more precise versions.
  • For arbitrary statements of Lean, I thought @Elliot Glazer has a conversion mechanism in mind to ZFC + the Parameter-Free Inaccessible Reflection Scheme (PFIRS). Here Elliot said "PFIRS proves an arbitrary sentence iff for some 𝑛, Lean proves that sentence holds in at least one of the first 𝑛 universes", but I'm a bit unclear on the details. Also, I think Elliot thinks one could mechanically extract a Lean proof into a corresponding proof in PFIRS even in such a way that you could check it in Metamath (using PFIRS axioms).

And obviously none of this is as important as just the consistency result.

I read that SE answer, and I don't think I care about PFIRS for the purpose of this proof. That's a matter of convenience for use in some later ZFC development, while I just want to measure lean against a known yardstick

Mario Carneiro said:

there is another map ZFC + omega inacc |- phi -> LeanTT |- g(phi), and probably the best you can hope for is LeanTT |- phi <-> g(f(phi))

Surely we can arrange that f and g are computable, injective, and satisfy that if ψ\psiψ is a subformula of ϕ\phiϕ, then ∥f(ψ)∥<∥f(ϕ)∥\|f(\psi)\| < \|f(\phi)\|∥f(ψ)∥<∥f(ϕ)∥ and ∥g(ψ)∥<∥g(ϕ)∥.\|g(\psi)\| < \|g(\phi)\|.∥g(ψ)∥<∥g(ϕ)∥. Then a Cantor-Bernstein construction gives us bijective such f and g where g=f−1.g=f^{-1}.g=f−1. Of course this is a grossly unnatural identification.

Let's instead restrict our attention to set theoretic formulas. In the ZFC context, that refers to arbitrary ϕ,\phi,ϕ, while in the Lean context, I mean assertions of the form ZFSet.{u} ⊨ϕ.\models \phi.⊨ϕ. The result @Jason Rute refers to is this: Let the Parameter-Free Inaccessible Reflection Scheme (PFIRS) be the schema of formulae of the form ϕ^:=ϕ→∃\hat{\phi}:=\phi \rightarrow \existsϕ^​:=ϕ→∃ inaccessible κ(ϕVκ).\kappa (\phi^{V_{\kappa}}).κ(ϕVκ​). Then ZFC + PFIRS proves ϕ\phiϕ iff for some n, LeanTT proves ⋁u<n\bigvee_{u<n}⋁u<n​ ZFSet.{u} ⊨ϕ.\models \phi.⊨ϕ.

Pf. ⇒\Rightarrow⇒ Let ϕ^0,…,ϕ^n−2\hat{\phi}_0, \ldots, \hat{\phi}_{n-2}ϕ^​0​,…,ϕ^​n−2​ be the instances of PFIRS used in a proof of some ϕ.\phi.ϕ. Notice each ϕ^i\hat{\phi}_iϕ^​i​ can only fail in at most one ZFSet.{u}, u<n, so at least one u<n satisfies all n-1 of these instances. ZFSet.{u} also satisfies ZFC, so ZFSet.{u} ⊨ϕ.\models \phi.⊨ϕ.

⇐\Leftarrow⇐ Suppose towards contradiction n is such that LeanTT proves ⋁u<n\bigvee_{u<n}⋁u<n​ ZFSet.{u} ⊨ϕ\models \phi⊨ϕ and T=ZFC+PFIRS+¬ϕ\neg \phi¬ϕ is consistent. Work in T. A simple induction shows that for all m, T proves that ¬ϕ\neg \phi¬ϕ holds in at least m universes. Consider the theory T' which results from appending to the language of T an ω\omegaω-sequence of constant symbols κi,\kappa_i,κi​, and to the theory the axioms of form "κi\kappa_iκi​ is an inaccessible" and for i<j,i<j,i<j, the axiom κi<κj.\kappa_i < \kappa_j.κi​<κj​. A compactness argument shows this is consistent, and this gives rise to a model of LeanTT where no universe satisfies ϕ,\phi,ϕ, contradicting the supposition. □\square□

ZFC+PFIRPS has the same Σ2\Sigma_2Σ2​ theorems ("local consequences") as ZFC+{n inaccessibles:n<ω}\{n \text{ inaccessibles}: n <\omega\}{n inaccessibles:n<ω} but even ZFC + TG axiom (a proper class of inaccessibles) fails to prove certain ϕ\phiϕ which provably hold in the first universe of Lean, such as "there is a Σ2\Sigma_2Σ2​-worldy cardinal." Thus if one wanted to build an automatic translator from Lean to some set theoretic library like Metamath's set.mm, PFIRS is the right addition to ZFC to be able to port propositions of arbitrary set-theoretic complexity.

And again, I don't mean to derail the main goal, namely that we can formally prove LeanTT is equiconsistent with ZFC + omega inacc. I mentioned the PFIRS stuff as an interesting consequence of this work that could be explored later (possibly in a different repo).

@Jason Rute How about just starting porting the proofs from rocq. Should not be too hard with AI...
#lean4lean > State of the Proof @ 💬

Hi @Bas Spitters. I assume you are talking about porting the ideas from Sets in Coq, Coq in Sets and the corresponding code in https://github.com/rocq-archive/zfc. (The link you gave in the other thread had a permission error.)

The way I assumed this would go is that Mario would create a repo with the main goal to complete, and I (or someone else) would help guide AI to fill it in (assuming Mario didn't just finish it start to end as he said he might if he has spare time). If I'm the one doing it, I'm probably happy to give the AI a pointer to "Sets in Coq, Coq in Set" paper (and maybe the repo) along with Mario's thesis.

But since Mario's model is straightforward, Mathlib already has a well-developed set theory library, and there are (possibly) major differences between the two set theoretic models (proof-irrelevance in the Lean model, cumulative hierarchy in the Rocq model, etc.), I don't know if the Rocq source material will be a lot of help in completing the goal (but maybe it is). (Also, I slightly worry about giving it the Rocq repo to do any kind of "direct port" since the source is LGPL-2.1 and Lean repos are typically Apache or MIT.)

Also, I'm afraid I may have oversold the amount of time I have to spend on this. I have a lot going on in my personal life at the moment. I have occasional bits of downtime to spend on things, but other days I have none. I don't want to commit to too much.
no problem, the repo will be there whenever you want to sink some tokens into it
https://github.com/digama0/lean4lean-model

I made https://github.com/digama0/lean4lean-model/pull/1, which adds a predicate for "uses certain axioms", and then weakened the (otherwise trivially false) headline theorem statement so it only talks about environments with the standard three axioms.

@Jason Rute I believe my question was mostly on how much the set theoretical models currently differ? (There are more set theoretical models of rocq's pCUIC). Rocq has a proof-irrelevant universe (sProp) too. Rocq is adopting algebraic universes (without imax) https://msp.cis.strath.ac.uk/types2025/abstracts/TYPES2025_paper21.pdf
@Mario Carneiro with your background from CMU, Chalmers, have you considered developing a categorical set theory to sit between ZFC and the interpretation from type theory?

The passage between categorical/structural set theories and material set theories is well-studied (cf work of Shulman that continues a long tradition of such, see his paper for citations), and the distance between type theory and categorical set theory is shorter, so I wholly endorse this idea, to the extent that means anything.
(off-topic, but I conjecture the complexity in the proof of relative consistency of NF is due to wanting to get a model of TST based on ZF(C), rather than a categorical set theory like ETCS)
(Maybe we could split this thread into "let's get lean4lean-model finished as is" and type theoretic questions?)

Got it. Closing https://github.com/digama0/lean4lean-model/pull/1, if I make progress on this I'll leave a sorry, and wait for you to update the statement to something true-y-er!

I reopened https://github.com/digama0/lean4lean-model/pull/1, with a version that allows the three standard axioms, checking not only their names and types, but that their types mean what they are meant to mean, i.e. the prerequisites have been installed correctly.

Just a working example, I think however you want to structure this should be easy to glue to.

https://github.com/digama0/lean4lean-model/pull/10 builds the set-theoretical model (including handling the standard axioms), ignoring everything do with with the inductive related sorries in lean4lean.

I haven't reviewed at all yet, so just consider this as a data point about what we can generate quickly. If anyone could review the shape, rather than the details of proofs, in case this is just going in the wrong direction?
(Oh, and there are some gaps related to how Quot.sound is handled in lean4lean, but the set theoretic model doesn't cheat here, I hope.)
